questions.question: Q: What is the key difference between a food allergy and a food intolerance?

points.text: A food allergy involves the immune system and can cause severe, life-threatening reactions (anaphylaxis). A food intolerance does not involve the immune system and typically causes less severe digestive symptoms.

questions.question: Q: What is coeliac disease and what diet must sufferers follow?

points.text: Coeliac disease is an autoimmune condition where gluten damages the lining of the small intestine, reducing nutrient absorption. Sufferers must follow a strict gluten-free diet, avoiding wheat, barley, and rye.

questions.question: Q: Why does lactose intolerance cause symptoms after consuming dairy?

points.text: People with lactose intolerance lack sufficient lactase enzyme to break down lactose (milk sugar). Undigested lactose ferments in the gut, causing bloating, diarrhoea, and stomach cramps.

questions.question: Q: What is the difference between a lacto-ovo vegetarian and a vegan?

points.text: A lacto-ovo vegetarian avoids meat, poultry, and fish but eats dairy products and eggs. A vegan excludes all animal products including dairy, eggs, honey, and animal-derived ingredients.

questions.question: Q: Name three common food allergies.

points.text: Peanuts, tree nuts, milk, eggs, fish, shellfish, soy, wheat, celery, sesame (any three).

questions.question: Q: What is anaphylaxis and how is it treated?

points.text: Anaphylaxis is a severe, life-threatening allergic reaction causing swelling of the airways, difficulty breathing, and a drop in blood pressure. It is treated with an adrenaline auto-injector (EpiPen).

questions.question: Q: Suggest a substitution for wheat flour in a recipe for someone with coeliac disease.

points.text: Gluten-free flour blends (rice flour, potato starch, tapioca flour, xanthan gum to replace gluten's binding properties).

questions.question: Q: Why must vegans ensure they get enough vitamin B12, iron, and calcium?

points.text: Vitamin B12 is found almost exclusively in animal products. Plant iron (non-haem) is less well absorbed than animal iron (haem). Dairy is a major calcium source, so vegans need fortified plant milks, tofu, or leafy greens.

markScheme.exemplarAnswer: A food allergy involves the immune system reacting to a specific food protein. Reactions can be immediate and severe, including swelling, difficulty breathing, and anaphylaxis (a life-threatening condition treated with adrenaline). Even trace amounts of the allergen can trigger a reaction. A food intolerance does not involve the immune system; it is a difficulty digesting certain foods, causing symptoms such as bloating, stomach cramps, and diarrhoea. Intolerances are generally less dangerous but can significantly affect quality of life. To adapt a cheese and pasta bake for someone with coeliac disease, I would replace wheat-based pasta with gluten-free pasta (made from rice, corn, or quinoa flour) and use a gluten-free flour blend to thicken the cheese sauce, adding xanthan gum to replace gluten's binding properties. I would also check that all other ingredients (stock, mustard, breadcrumb topping) are gluten-free, as even small amounts of gluten can cause damage. For someone with lactose intolerance, I would replace the cow's milk in the sauce with lactose-free milk or a plant-based alternative such as oat milk, and substitute the cheese with lactose-free cheese or a small amount of mature hard cheese (which contains minimal lactose). These adaptations ensure the dish is safe for both conditions while maintaining similar flavour and texture.
